documents: Wysocka et al. (2022) The Hoanh Bo Trough-a landward keyhole to the syn-rift Late Eocene–Early Oligocene terrestrial succession of the northern Song Hong Basin. Geological Journal 57:4216–4241 (published PDF)

entry.evidence: there is still a need for a coherent model describing the origin and evolution of the tectonically influenced Palaeogene sedimentary system

steps.action: Authors state the gap in onshore Palaeogene basin models and set the aim: recognize the sedimentary pattern, infill age and clastic sources of the Hoanh Bo Trough.
steps.quote: there is still a need for a coherent model describing the origin and evolution of the tectonically influenced Palaeogene sedimentary system

steps.action: Authors state the hypothesis that the Hoanh Bo Trough is a landward analogue for contemporaneous offshore basins, especially the northern Song Hong Basin.
steps.quote: the hypothesis that the Hoanh Bo Trough could be treated as a landward analogue for contemporaneous offshore basins

steps.action: Archival descriptions of the Dong Ho and Tieu Giao formations are compared with field observations, found not to match, and set aside in favour of the authors' own description.
steps.quote: are similar and do not exactly align with field observations

steps.action: Field observations, measurements and sampling from 2013–2014, with preliminary lithofacies and petrographic results, were done and published in the authors' earlier work.
steps.quote: preliminary lithofacies, sedimentary environment, and petrographic results were published by Tha et al. (2015, 2017)

steps.action: Outcrops at 82 localities in seven sections and archival logs of 12 wells are logged. In 2019, nine fine-grained samples are processed for palynology (HCl/HF maceration, counts of at least 100 grains) and six for LA–ICP–MS bulk geochemistry.
steps.quote: Observations were made from 82 localities in total and supplemented by archival data from 12 wells (Hoa & Phong, 1960)

steps.action: Seventeen lithofacies (Miall codes) are identified and grouped into six facies associations, each assigned a depositional environment from proximal alluvial fan to lacustrine.
steps.quote: based on the coexistence of particular lithofacies in outcrops and wells, six facies associations were distinguished

steps.action: Palynomorph percentages are reported for four productive samples (angiosperm-dominated), together with major, trace and REE geochemistry, a Herron classification and chondrite-normalized REE patterns.
steps.quote: only four, taken from the Le Loi, Yen My, and Gieng Day sections in the Hoanh Bo area, contained sufficient identifiable palynomorphs

steps.action: From surface facies distribution (a coarsening-up northern flank and monomictic fans on the western flank), authors propose a trough bordered by active faults to the north and west.
steps.quote: it is reasonable to suggest that the study area was a trough bordered by active fault escapements to the north and west

steps.action: The surface-based hypothesis is checked against the independent archival well data and a 3-D map of the Triassic basement surface, which shows steep relief and fine-grained facies at the base of the wells.
steps.quote: This hypothesis can be verified and supplemented by the archival well data.

steps.action: Authors retain the interpretation that all strata were deposited in a single basin that was later uplifted, tilted, faulted and eroded.
steps.quote: the strata examined in the Hoanh Bo Trough were deposited in a single sedimentary basin

steps.action: Published southern-China palynostratigraphy is used to set expectations for Late Eocene assemblages: Fagaceae tricolp(or)ate grains, porate Alnus, Ulmus, Juglandaceae and Myricaceae.
steps.quote: the prevalence of tricolpate and tricolporate grains belonging to Fagaceae is considered to be indicative of a Late Eocene age

steps.action: The studied assemblages are compared with the Late Eocene expectation: Fagaceae match, but Alnus is absent and other expected families are rare.
steps.quote: Ulmus is present in two samples, Alnus is absent

steps.action: The Alnus mismatch is absorbed by an auxiliary (azonal or edaphic control on Alnus, citing Bose Basin zones without Alnipollenites) rather than by revising the age.
steps.quote: the absence of Alnus pollen in the assemblages studied herein does not necessarily pose issues in defining the age

steps.action: The assemblages are compared with Xie et al.'s Late Eocene characteristics (high Quercoideae, increased Pinuspollenites) and found consistent.
steps.quote: This is markedly consistent with the palynological assemblages obtained in the present study

steps.action: Palaeoclimate is inferred from thermophilous palaeotropical taxa, after accounting for over-representation of wind-pollinated taxa, as very warm tropical or subtropical.
steps.quote: is proof that the climate was very warm–probably, tropical or subtropical

steps.action: A purely Oligocene (or younger) age is argued against because regional Oligocene floras, such as the independently dated Lühe Basin flora, are warm-temperate and lack tropical elements.
steps.quote: more consistent with a Late Eocene age, rather than an Oligocene age

steps.action: Sample 54 resembles Latest Eocene/Early Oligocene floras, so the age is refined to Late Eocene–Early Oligocene at youngest; a separate age for that sample is declined because its stratigraphic position is unknown.
steps.quote: it would be highly hazardous to unilaterally declare that sample ID 54 is of a considerably different age

steps.action: The Late Eocene–Early Oligocene age is retained against earlier Oligocene/Miocene datings, and the Dong Ho and Tieu Giao formations are synonymized as the Dong Ho Formation.
steps.quote: are herein synonymized as the Dong Ho Formation

steps.action: Source rock is inferred from trace-element discrimination diagrams and REE ratios as a silicic, post-Archean felsic protolith, with recycling from older sedimentary rocks shown by Th/Sc–Zr/Sc and Al–Zr–Ti trends.
steps.quote: Trace element analysis suggests that all studied samples were derived from silicic source rocks

steps.action: Recycling trends are compared with published data from the Na Duong, Cao Bang and Truc Thon basins; the Hoanh Bo samples come out less intensively recycled.
steps.quote: Data from the Palaeogene Na Duong and Cao Bang Basins and the Pleistocene Truc Thon Basin are plotted for comparison

steps.action: The lower-recycling inference is checked with a second method, sandstone petrography (crystalline lithoclasts, some feldspar).
steps.quote: This is supported by the petrographic study of sandstones in the present study

steps.action: Weathering intensity and humidity are estimated with an A–CN–K diagram and the CIA, CIW, PIA, ICV and CIA molar indices, giving tropical humid conditions for Dong Ho and subtropical for Hoanh Bo.
steps.quote: were used to estimate the degree of weathering of the source rocks

steps.action: The geochemical climate inference is compared with the independent palynological climate inference, and the two agree.
steps.quote: These claims are in reasonable agreement with the climatic conclusions reached from palynomorph analyses

steps.action: The inferred tropical-to-subtropical shift is compared with the published global cooling at the Eocene/Oligocene transition.
steps.quote: [...] with the postulated global cooling at the Eocene/Oligocene climatic transition

steps.action: Basin evolution is reconstructed as a transtensional half-graben between the active Trung Luong and Chi Linh–Dong Trieu–Hon Gai faults, passing from lake-dominated to fluvial and alluvial-fan-dominated fill.
steps.quote: it evolved in a transtensional setting

steps.action: The Holz et al. (2017) conceptual model of tectonic system tracts in continental rifts is taken as the expectation.
steps.quote: According to the conceptual model for the sequence stratigraphy of continental rift successions introduced by Holz

steps.action: The facies succession is matched to the rift initiation, rift development and rift termination system tracts.
steps.quote: succession matches well with tectonic system tracts

steps.action: The interpretation is compared with published Song Hong Basin rifting history and with seismic interpretations of the undrilled offshore Kien An Basin (Fyhn et al. 2018, 2020).
steps.quote: The above interpretation is quite consistent with data on Palaeogene rifting in the Song Hong Basin.

steps.action: Authors retain the claim that the Hoanh Bo Trough is an onshore, well-exposed analogue (landward keyhole) for the offshore sub-basins of the Song Hong Basin.
steps.quote: the Hoanh Bo Trough may be treated as an onshore, well-exposed analogue for the offshore sub-basins

Facies are observed directly; age, provenance, climate and basin evolution are inferred from traces
Characterize sedimentary pattern, age and sources; test the offshore-analogue hypothesis
Earlier Oligocene/Miocene dating versus a Late Eocene–Early Oligocene age

Conditions found in outcrops and archival wells, not set

Partly: well data, petrography and cross-proxy climate agreement; age rests on 4 samples
Single syn-rift basin of Late Eocene–Early Oligocene age kept as landward keyhole
Referees acknowledged; review record not supplied

end.claim: The Hoanh Bo Trough is a single fault-bounded syn-rift basin filled in the Late Eocene–Early Oligocene with lacustrine-to-fluvial deposits flanked by alluvial fans, and can be treated as a landward keyhole for offshore basins such as the Kien An Basin of the northern Song Hong Basin.

decisive_move.sentence: The reconstruction of facies associations and basin architecture from outcrops and wells, joined to the palynological age that places the infill in the syn-rift Late Eocene–Early Oligocene, is what lets the trough be matched with the offshore rift basins.

gates.evidence: Action: the analogue hypothesis is stated in the Introduction (p. 4217), but the 2019 sampling was motivated by earlier findings and the general aim to characterize the basin (p. 4220). Claim: the age faced expectations from published assemblages; a mismatch (Alnus absent) was absorbed by an auxiliary (p. 4232). The surface fault-bounded trough hypothesis was checked against well data (p. 4229). The analogue claim rests on qualitative matching (pp. 4236–4237). Registration: nothing is reported as fixed before the data.

imports.item: Laser ablation–inductively coupled plasma–mass spectrometry (LA–ICP–MS) at a commercial laboratory
Nearest-living-relative assignment of fossil pollen taxa
Over-representation of anemophilous versus entomophilous taxa in pollen records

novelty_claims.quote: For the first time, these results have been placed within the context of regional geology and Palaeogene climate change in northern Vietnam.

limits: Authors call the age results very preliminary. The age rests on four productive, poorly preserved pollen samples, with no direct biostratigraphic control (dinocysts, foraminifera) and no radiometric dating (p. 4230). The stratigraphic positions of the samples in the composite section are unknown (p. 4232). Geochemistry uses six samples. Well data are archival (1960) and their re-examination is not described. A 'petrographic study' is invoked as support (p. 4234) but its data are not shown in the main text (inference). Internal tension: section 4.4 states no evidence of fault activity to the south (p. 4229), and the Conclusions describe a trough bordered from the north and west (p. 4237), while section 5.3 and Figure 14a describe an active southern margin (p. 4235). The analogue claim compares against seismic-only interpretations of the undrilled Kien An Basin (p. 4237). Sub-claim statuses: facies associations, best_explanation; Late Eocene–Early Oligocene age and formation synonymy, best_explanation (preliminary); felsic recycled provenance, best_explanation; tropical-to-subtropical climate shift, best_explanation. The age revision against earlier Oligocene/Miocene dating could be read as outcome 'contradicted', but the authors present it as preliminary; coded kept. A peer review history exists (Publons) but was not supplied, so no review sequence is coded.

disagreements.support: Palynological assemblages compared with dated southern-China Late Eocene and Oligocene floras point to a Late Eocene–Early Oligocene age.
disagreements.quote: is not in agreement with previous dating efforts suggesting the sediments were deposited during Oligocene/Miocene

disagreements.target: Lithostratigraphic subdivision into Dong Ho and Tieu Giao formations (Nhan & Danh 1975; Thanh & Khuc 2006)
disagreements.support: Field descriptions do not support the subdivision, and both units share the same Late Eocene–Early Oligocene age, so they are synonymized.
disagreements.quote: we suggest there is no need to distinguish the Dong Ho and Tieu Giao formations

disagreements.target: Archival descriptions of the Dong Ho and Tieu Giao formations
disagreements.support: Direct field observations do not match the archival descriptions.
disagreements.quote: are similar and do not exactly align with field observations

disagreements.target: Late Eocene pollen criteria emphasizing Alnus and porate taxa (Song et al. 2010; Ye et al. 1996; Alexandrova et al. [...]
disagreements.support: Bose Basin Late Eocene zones lacking Alnipollenites (Liu & Yang 1999) suggest the absence of Alnus is local or edaphic and not diagnostic of age.
disagreements.quote: representatives of the other two families are rare–in stark contrast to what would be expected based on the studies described above
